issues.description: Regex `/\dm?s/i` is a coarse over-approximation that can match non-time substrings inside URLs, strings, or identifiers.
issues.detail: The pre-filter fires on any digit adjacent to `s`/`ms`, so values like `url(foo1s.png)` or `"abc1ms"` still hit the slow path. Correctness is preserved because valueParser runs after, but the predicate is weaker than its name suggests. Rename toward `MAY_CONTAIN_TIME` or add a one-line comment marking it as a deliberate cheap pre-filter.

issues.description: No regression test pins the early-return behavior against awkward inputs.
issues.detail: The change alters which declarations reach valueParser, but no fixture exercises the suspect cases: time tokens inside `url()`, quoted strings, custom-property names containing `ms`, vendor prefixes, or unusual whitespace/casing. A small set of fixtures would lock in equivalence with the prior implementation and guard the fast path. Not blocking.

synthesis.summary: The panel accepts this as a clean, small, data-driven performance patch: a cheap regex gate short-circuits the expensive valueParser path when no time-like token is present, and reordering `vendor.unprefixed`/`toLowerCase` below the guard avoids needless work. Correctness is preserved because the regex is an over-approximation and the real parser still validates anything that passes. The only consensus nits are P2: the predicate's name overstates what it decides and deserves a one-line comment, and a regression fixture should pin the early-return against tricky inputs like time-looking substrings in URLs or strings. Land it with the trivial fixups.
